title: Medical model training changed privacy risk more than who ranked highest
summary: Across six clinical datasets, privacy-risk rankings were broadly similar under many changes to model training. In one chest X-ray cohort, stronger regularization reduced the share of patients above the study’s risk threshold from 88% to 30%. The rankings were compared across training changes using an audit of 7,789 medical-model instances.
ai_technology: ResNet, EfficientNet, vision transformers, ECGFounder, MRI-CORE
organization: University of Crete; Foundation for Research and Technology–Hellas; University of Maryland

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 PDF affiliation, aggregate Figures 2 and 4, cohort and risk-stability comparison

evidence.tested: A defensive study compared aggregate risk distributions and ordinal stability under seed, architecture, regularization and fine-tuning changes, including comparisons with trained seed replicates.
evidence.unknown: The outcomes measure estimated likelihood of training-set membership disclosure under the study’s audit. They do not represent observed patient disclosures or complete invariance across all settings.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers trained several thousand medical-model instances, including ECGFounder and MRI-CORE adaptations, and compared aggregate distributions of measured privacy risk across training regimes.
